cards.explanation: The answer is that the Day of the LORD is coming. The horn sounds because "…the Day of the LORD is coming…" and Joel adds that it is near. That is a wake-up call, friends, not a background song. When the alarm goes off for this reason, everybody in the land is supposed to hear it.

The answer is False. Joel describes "…a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness." That is about as far from a beach forecast as you can get, friends. Nobody is planning a picnic for this day.

The answer is that there has never been an army like it. Joel says this army is "…such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come." Not before, not after, friends. It is the only one of its kind.

The answer is that the land behind them is like a desert wasteland. Joel says the land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them it is like a desert wasteland. Lush on the way in, bare on the way out, friends. That's a hard change to look at.
The answer is True. Joel says "…surely nothing will escape them." He doesn't say most things or a few things, friends. Nothing.
The answer is that they writhe in horror. Joel says "Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale." That's a whole room of people going white at once, friends. Nobody is acting casual.

The answer is False. Joel says "They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path." He compares them to mighty men and men of war, and each one keeps to his own path. Not a step out of place, friends.
The answer is through the windows like thieves. Joel says they climb into houses "…entering through windows like thieves." Windows are how this army gets in, friends. That's the way they come.
The answer is dark. Joel says "The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness." Sun, moon and stars all lose their light, friends. That's a sky I wouldn't want to look at.
The answer is the LORD's. Joel says "The LORD raises His voice in the presence of His army." So this is His army and His voice, friends. That changes how you read everything before it.
The answer is to return to Him with all your heart. The LORD says, "Yet even now," and then "return to Me with all your heart…" The words "even now" matter here, friends. The door isn't shut.
The answer is hearts. Joel says "So rend your hearts and not your garments…" Rend means tear, friends. The point is the inside, not the show on the outside.

The answer is gracious and slow to anger. Joel says "…He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion." That's the reason he gives to return, friends. It's a God worth coming back to.
The answer is True. Joel says "And He relents from sending disaster." That sits in the same breath as gracious and compassionate, friends.
The answer is a blessing. Joel says He may "…leave a blessing behind Him…" Notice he starts with "Who knows?" and says "may," friends. So Joel isn't promising it, but he is pointing toward it.

The answer is a fast and a sacred assembly. Joel says "…consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly." The horn is calling people to come together before the LORD, friends. Verse 1 also speaks of blowing the ram's horn in Zion, and here the call is for a fast and an assembly.

The answer is False. Joel says "Gather the people…" and then names the aged, the children, and even those nursing at the breast. He adds the bridegroom and the bride too, friends. Nobody gets to say it's a meeting for somebody else.
The answer is to spare His people. The priests are to say "Spare Your people, O LORD…" Joel gives them the words to say, friends. They weep and they ask.

The answer is "Where is their God?" The priests say, "Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’…" That's the question they don't want echoing among the nations, friends. They ask the LORD not to let His people become an object of scorn.
